decisive_items: elevated transprosthetic gradients (mean 33 mmHg) with an effective orifice area index of 0.4 cm2/m2 (suggesting severe prosthesis–patient mismatch)
response.rationale: Severe prosthesis-patient mismatch directly explains persistent dyspnea despite decongestion and is supported by objective echo findings; high-output state may coexist but does not negate the hemodynamically significant mismatch. HFpEF was only initial and less specific given normal wedge pressure.

rejected.why: Severe tricuspid regurgitation is a consequence of pulmonary hypertension/volume overload, not the primary unifying diagnosis.
The liver lesion is an incidental finding; it does not explain the acute cardiopulmonary presentation or catheterization data.
Initial label only; right heart catheterization shows only slight wedge elevation, inconsistent with typical HFpEF.
